title: Tea Production — Kenya and East Africa Highlands
content:
## Tea (Camellia sinensis) — East Africa

Kenya is the world's third-largest tea exporter. Smallholder tea is organized through factories under KTDA (Kenya Tea Development Agency) in Kenya.

### Growing Zones

- **Optimal altitude:** 1500–2700m (Kericho, Nandi, Nyamira, Limuru, Tanzania Southern Highlands, Rwanda, Burundi)
- **Rainfall:** 1200–1400mm/year, well distributed
- **Soil:** Deep, well-drained acidic volcanic soils (pH 4.5–5.5)

### Recommended Clones (Kenya — TRFK/KALRO)

- **TRFK 6/8** — high yield, good quality
- **TRFK 31/8** — drought tolerant
- **TRFK 303/577** — resistant to root diseases
- **BBK 35** — popular in smallholder blocks

### Planting and Management

- Spacing: 1.2m × 0.75m (≈11,000 bushes/ha)
- Pluck to 'two leaves and a bud' — standard for quality black tea
- Plucking round: 7–14 days depending on season
- Fertilizer: NPK 26:5:5 or tea-specific blends at 200–400 kg/ha/year split across rains
- Prune every 3–4 years (maintenance prune) to rejuvenate bushes

### Key Diseases

Tea leaf rust, blister blight, and root rot — see tea disease entries. Report severe outbreaks to factory extension officer.

## Chai (Camellia sinensis) Afrika Mashariki

Kenya ni mtumaji wa tatu duniani wa chai. Wakulima wadogo huuza chai kupitia vianda vya KTDA.

### Maeneo Bora

- **Mwinuko:** 1500–2700m (Kericho, Nandi, Limuru)
- **Mvua:** mm 1200–1400 kwa mwaka
- **Udongo:** volkeni, unaoelea vizuri, pH 4.5–5.5

### Upanzi

- Umbali: mita 1.2 × 0.75
- Chuma majani mawili na budi
- Mbolea: NPK 26:5:5 kilo 200–400/hekta kwa mwaka

title: Tea Leaf Rust — Exobasidium vexans
content:
## Tea Leaf Rust (Exobasidium vexans)

Tea leaf rust is a fungal disease affecting tea bushes in humid highland areas of Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.

### Symptoms

- Pale yellow or white spots on upper leaf surface
- Orange-yellow powdery pustules on underside of young leaves (key ID feature)
- Affected leaves become thick and distorted
- Severe infection reduces photosynthesis and yield 15–30%
- Most damaging on young flush leaves during wet season

### Conditions Favoring Rust

- High humidity (>85%), frequent mist/rain
- Shaded areas with poor air circulation
- Overgrown, unpruned bushes

### Management

- **Cultural:** Improve plucking to remove infected flush; prune to open canopy; maintain drainage
- **Chemical:** Copper oxychloride 3 kg/ha or Hexaconazole 250 ml/ha — apply at first sign, repeat every 21 days in wet season
- **Resistant clones:** TRFK 31/8 and some regional clones show tolerance
- Coordinate sprays with factory field officer — harvest withholding periods apply

### Distinguishing from Other Tea Problems

| Problem | Key feature |
|---------|-------------|
| Tea leaf rust | Orange powder underside of young leaves |
| Blister blight | Translucent blisters, no orange powder |
| Red spider mite | Bronzing, fine webbing, no pustules |
content_sw:
## Kutu ya Majani ya Chai (Tea Leaf Rust)

Ugonjwa wa kuvu unaosumbua chai milimani Kenya na Tanzania.

### Dalili

- Madoa ya manjano au nyeupe juu ya jani
- Unyevu wa rangi ya machungwa chini ya jani (dalili muhimu)
- Majani yanakonda na kupunguza mavuno

### Kudhibiti

- Chuma majani yaliyoathirika; panga mimea
- Dawa ya shaba au Hexaconazole kila wiki 3 wakati wa mvua
- Wasiliana na afisa wa kampuni ya chai
